To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the development of integrative processes depends on the fulfillment of psychological needs; (2) these needs are not always fulfilled, and the degree to which they are met varies across individuals, situations, and domains; (3) the degree to which needs are fulfilled is influenced by the nature of the individual's social context and by the nature of his or her social interactions with others; (4) the fulfillment of psychological need is not a sufficient condition for the development of integrativeness;
psychological needs facilitate integrative processes, and that the absence of need satisfaction forestalls these processes.

the degree of integration of the personality and the degree of internalization of socialization goals are positively correlated with the extent to which the individual experiences the context as supporting the fulfillment of basic psychological needs for autonomy (i.e., choice and self-direction), competence (i.e., effectiveness), and relatedness (i.e., caring and concern).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of psychological needs and their social supports in the development of personality, motivation, and social relations.
the conditions under which people experience themselves as relatively unified and integrated.
the facilitation of intrapsychic integration, the development of self, and the promotion of positive psychological health and well-being.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
integrative processes are not automatic, nor are they nonexistent.
integrative tendencies and the psychological needs they depend upon are central to the study of human motivation and development, and to the understanding of human nature.
the facilitation of psychological needs for autonomy and relatedness are critical to integrative processes. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2005 APA, all rights reserved)
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
integrative processes are facilitated by social conditions that fulfill basic psychological needs for autonomy and relatedness.
psychological needs are a central factor in the facilitation of integration. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2006 APA, all rights reserved)
integrative tendencies are not innate but are facilitated by conditions that meet basic human psychological needs for autonomy and relatedness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
integrative tendencies are not automatic or innate but are facilitated by social contexts that support the satisfaction of psychological needs.
integrative tendencies are dynamic and dependent on social contextual supports.
